channel.title: Practical Rewards Blog
channel.description: Straight answers about credit cards, points, cash back, and the fine print.

item.title: Cents Per Point Explained: What 4x Points Is Actually Worth
item.description: Learn how to calculate cents per point, turn earning multipliers into useful comparisons, and avoid chasing redemption values you would never pay cash for.

item.title: Cash Back or Points? Start With the Work You’ll Actually Do
item.description: Points can deliver outsized value, but transfers take research. Learn what points mean and how to compare their real return with cash back.

item.title: The Boring 2% Card Is the Right First Card
item.description: Start with a flat 2% card: choose cash back or travel rewards, then keep 2% as the floor for ordinary spending.

item.title: Monthly Card Credits Are a Part-Time Job
item.description: Rate card credits by expiration, restrictions, booking steps, and realistic use—not the headline value.

item.title: The Sapphire Reserve’s DoorDash credits are mostly not for takeout
item.description: The Sapphire Reserve’s three monthly DoorDash benefits rise to $35 on October 1, while DashPass remains a separate perk.

item.title: The Organic Spend Test: Would You Buy It Without the Card?
item.description: Use the organic spend test to separate useful card credits from coupons that encourage unnecessary spending.

item.title: Amex Platinum’s $300 Lululemon credit still leaves $595 to justify
item.description: The Amex Platinum now offers $75 in quarterly Lululemon credits, but even full use leaves $595 of its annual fee to justify.

item.title: Your Annual Fee Isn’t the Number That Matters
item.description: Calculate a credit card’s effective annual fee using only credits you would genuinely use, then repeat the math at every renewal.
